proof.criterion: Item 3: the tautology test is gone and a planReplay check replaces it

proof.observed: TestReplayEventTypeConstants, which compared each constant with the literal beside it, is gone. TestReplayPlannerHandlesEveryTypeItNames replaces it: it sends one event of every type planWrite handles through planReplay and fails on any 'unhandled:' reason or a transaction count below one per type. A wording point for whoever next edits the README or stack.sh, not a failure and not one of the six: LOADTEST_PG_PORT moves a port only through stack.sh setup, because start reads the ports stack.json records. My first attempt at the third refusal set the variable on start alone, and the refusal correctly named the recorded port instead. One of the three refusal branches says 'set LOADTEST_PG_PORT and rerun stack.sh setup' and the other two say only 'set LOADTEST_PG_PORT to a port no one holds'; naming the setup rerun in all three would save the next reader that step.

Three event-type constants, evMessageDelivery, evMessageAccepted and evPrefixUserState, can be misspelt with the whole suite still green. All three name events the replay never sends, and a misspelt evMessageDelivery leaves replay-plan's counts byte-identical over the real bundle, so nothing a run does depends on them. Recorded because a later change could give one of them a part in what is sent, and the test that would catch it is the bundle-driven one, which needs LOADTEST_REPLAY_BUNDLE and does not run in CI.
